title: Container with Most Water
summary: Each array entry gives the height of a vertical line at its zero-based index.
statement: Each array entry gives the height of a vertical line at its zero-based index. Choose two lines as the sides of an upright container. Return the largest area it can hold. For indices i and j with i < j, the width is j − i and the water level is limited by the shorter line.

examples.explanation: The outer walls give width 2 and height 4.
The walls at indices 1 and 3 give width 2 and height 6.
The shorter line has height zero.

hints: Conceptual: A tall line cannot raise the water level above the shorter side.
Directional: Start with the widest pair. Moving the taller side alone cannot improve the area of that pair.
Implementation: Record the current area and move the shorter side inward. Either side can move on a tie.
complexityAnalysis: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space. Each comparison moves a pointer inward.
